# Parameter modes (In, Out, InOut)

@difference Extension: function parameters can be written as `In`, `Out` or `InOut`, which decides if a value goes into the function, comes back out of it, or both.

In the originals every parameter is passed by value: the function gets a copy, and changing it never reaches the caller. BlitzLLVM keeps that as the default (`In`), and adds two words in front of a parameter name to hand values back to the caller.

```blitzbasic
Function Swap(InOut a:Int32, InOut b:Int32)
	Local t:Int32 = a
	a = b
	b = t
End Function

Function Split(value:Int32, Out high:Int32, Out low:Int32)
	high = value / 256
	low = value Mod 256
End Function

Local x:Int32 = 1, y:Int32 = 2
Swap x, y        ; x is 2, y is 1
Split 1000, x, y ; x is 3, y is 232
```

## The three modes

| Mode | Starts with | Written values reach the caller | Must be written |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `In` (default) | the value of the caller | no | no |
| `Out` | the default value of the type (`0`, `0.0`, `""`, `Null`) | yes | yes, on every path (an error otherwise) |
| `InOut` | the value of the caller | yes | should be (warning `inout-parameter-unwritten`, level 3) |

All three can be read and written inside of the function, the word only decides what is passed along. `Function Name(In a:Int32)` is the same as `Function Name(a:Int32)`. The words are only special in front of a parameter name, so `In`, `Out` and `InOut` can still be used as names of variables and parameters.

The values are copied back when the function returns, not while it runs, so a function that calls itself works on its own copy at every level, and the caller only sees the result at the end. If the same variable is given to two `Out` or `InOut` parameters, the last parameter wins.

## What the caller can pass

`Out` and `InOut` need something to write to: a variable (local or global), an element of an array, or a field of an object. The compiler refuses a constant, a number, a string, a call or any other expression, a whole array, and a variable of another type than the parameter (`Out x:Int32` does not take a `Float32`, as the value could not be stored back unchanged). `In` parameters accept everything they always did.

Strings are copied like everywhere else, objects are passed as the handle to the object, so an `Out b.Box` can be given a `New Box` and the caller has it afterwards.

## Default values

A parameter with `= value` can be left out by the caller. For `Out`, the default is applied before the function body runs (so `Out x:Int32 = 5` starts with 5, also when the caller passes a variable). For `InOut`, the default is used when the caller leaves the argument out; otherwise the function starts with the caller's value. A parameter that is left out has no variable to write back to, and the function just works on its own copy.

## Writing on every path

An `Out` parameter has to be written before every `Return` and before the end of the function, or the compiler stops with an error naming the place. For `InOut` the same check is the warning `inout-parameter-unwritten` (`-W3`), reported once for every `Return` (or end of function) that leaves without writing. What counts as writing: an assignment, being the counter of a `For`, being the target of `Read`, or handing it to an `Out` or `InOut` parameter of another function. A path that ends the program (`End`) does not count, and writing only inside of one branch of an `If` without an `Else` (or a `Select` without `Default`, a `While` or a `For`, which may run zero times) does not either. Functions that use `Goto` or `Gosub` are not checked.

```blitzbasic
Function Clamp(Out result:Int32, value:Int32)
	If value > 10 Then
		result = 10
	EndIf
	; Error: 'result' is not written when value is 10 or less
End Function
```

## Not available

`.decls` libraries (Userlibs) keep their own way of passing values and do not use these words. `Void` functions can use them like any other function.
